title: Indigo Labs — Onboarding Immersion Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Indigo Labs onboarding to align runtime requirements, security review path, and pilot success criteria. Covered deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), performance expectations, initial integration plan, and observability runbook. Agreed on benchmark pilot and security package delivery.
topics: Deployment modes: hosted, dedicated, private VPC
Initial pilot scope and success metrics (latency, cost target, 95th pct)
Security & compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
Networking: egress, peering, IP allowlists, and firewall rules
Observability / tracing / cost dashboards and per-route breakouts
Rollout plan: canary, A/B, auto-fallback to smaller model variant
action_items: Priya Rao (Redwood) — Share security package (SOC2 report, ISO summary, data flow diagram) by 2027-08-27
Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE) — Run initial latency/cost benchmark using Indigo sample prompt set and send results by 2027-09-02
Sanjay Patel (Indigo) — Provide sample prompt corpus and expected QPS profile by 2027-08-30

Olivia Park (Indigo PM) — Finalize pilot success criteria doc (SLOs + business KPIs) by 2027-08-31
next_steps: Redwood to deliver security folder and runbook link (secure link) — due 2027-08-27

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-08-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao (Redwood) — Sanjay Patel, Maya Chen, Ethan Ross, Olivia Park (Indigo Labs)

Summary section (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood walked through onboarding steps and observed constraints; customer emphasized tight latency budget for interactive experience and need for VPC/on-prem options for regulated datasets. Action items captured.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll run through the agenda real quick — intro, roles, what success looks like, then Liam will go into the tech plan and benchmarks.
[00:22] Sanjay (Indigo CTO): Thanks Sofia, quick note — we have legal on the line sometimes but today it's just the core tech crew. We're excited to get this moving.
[00:35] Liam (Redwood SE): Hi team, I'm Liam, I'll be your SE for the pilot; quick note on what we'll test: latency 95th < 350ms for our sample chat workflows, cost per 1k tokens target we'll correlate with Redwood Optimize suggestions.
[00:58] Maya (Head of ML): That's, uh, roughly our target. We also need to ensure the KV cache and prefix caching match our session lengths — lots of multi-turn.
[01:15] Olivia (PM): And from product side we need deterministic rollbacks if quality regresses during canary.
[01:27] Priya (CSM): We'll own the onboarding cadence, weekly sync and escalation points. I'll include a template for the rollout runbook.
[01:40] Ethan (SRE): For networking, can you outline VPC peering and IP ranges we need? Also curious about private deployment options — we have sensitive PII in some flows.
[01:58] Sofia: Yes, we'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private. Quick primer: hosted for fastest start, dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, private (VPC/on-prem) when you need customer-controlled network and keys.
[02:18] Sanjay: Does Redwood offer HSM/KMS integration? We need envelope encryption so logs don't contain keys.
[02:28] Liam: Yes, we support KMS integrations and can show our key rotation policies. Also audit logs are available — we'll include the schema in the security pack.
[02:40] Maya: On the model side, do you have recommendations for quantization or model variants for latency/cost tradeoffs?
[02:49] Liam: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles; for inference we can route to smaller variants automatically if we see SLO pressure. There's also an option for continuous batching tuning.
[03:10] Olivia: Can you explain the fallback policies — like if Dedicated runs out of capacity?
[03:18] Sofia: We have smart routing: policy-based routing by latency/cost/region. If a pool is constrained, we can fallback to compatible model variants or a hosted fallback. We'll capture the policy in the runbook.
[03:33] Sanjay: Great, show of hands — who on Indigo will provide sample prompts?
[03:40] Maya: We'll export a representative prompt corpus (priority intents, average length, and 99th pct length) and share it.
[03:47] Liam: Perfect — that'll feed into batching and kernel selection for the bench.
[03:55] Speaker 6: (background) mm-hmm, okay.
[04:02] Priya: Security steps — we'll send SOC2, ISO summary, subprocessor list, and a short DFD. Expect that in a secure folder link.
[04:12] Ethan: Do you have any customers in our vertical who used private deployment?
[04:19] Sofia: A few regulated customers have used private VPC deployments; we can redact names in the security whitepaper but provide patterns and anonymized references.
[04:31] Sanjay: On connectivity, we might prefer peering rather than open egress — what's typical?
[04:38] Liam: Peering is common for lower latency and predictable egress; we document IP ranges and peering steps. Also, allowlist for webhooks and callbacks.
[04:52] Olivia: Observability — what will the console show us out of the box?
[04:57] Priya: Console has per-route token breakdown, latency histograms, and per-route cost. We can enable longer retention for an enterprise add-on if you need it.
[05:09] Maya: We'll need tracing — correlating request IDs with our APM.
[05:14] Liam: Yes, we provide trace hooks and headers you can forward into your APM. We'll show an example instrumentation snippet.
[05:30] Sanjay: About the pilot: how long is the pilot and what signifies success?
[05:36] Sofia: Typically pilots run 4–6 weeks; success criteria we usually structure as: latency SLOs, accuracy/quality checks against a closed prompt set, and cost thresholds. Olivia, can you draft the KPIs?
[05:48] Olivia: Yep, I'll draft and share by the end of the week.
[05:53] Maya: Also we want to run a performance regression eval — a small quality harness against our golden prompts.
[05:59] Liam: We'll help wire that into Redwood's evals and alert on regressions.
[06:10] Ethan: Any special prod-like test for KV cache invalidation? We have multi-turn dialogs where context size changes.
[06:18] Liam: We'll include scenarios for cache warm/cold in the bench. Good call.
[06:26] Sanjay: Pricing question — if we go dedicated, how does billing handle burst?
[06:32] Sofia: Dedicated has reserved base throughput and optional burst capacity; we'll include a pricing appendix and show estimated unit economics from your sample QPS.
[06:43] Sanjay: Can we see a sample cost breakdown per feature?
[06:47] Priya: Yes, we'll provide a token-level cost breakout per route and a pro forma for dedicated commit levels.
[06:56] (silence / typing)
[07:05] Maya: On the security docs — will you include a table of logs retained and where they land? We need to verify PII handling.
[07:12] Liam: We'll include retention periods and log redaction options — you can turn off full-text retention for sensitive flows.
[07:21] Olivia: For SSO, we use SAML with SCIM for provisioning — is that supported?
[07:27] Sofia: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; we'll share a connection guide.
[07:34] Ethan: Do you integrate with our internal KMS (cloud vendor) or do you need a separate Redwood-managed key?
[07:42] Liam: We can integrate with customer-managed KMS and show the handshake.
[07:48] Sanjay: Let's talk timelines — we want pilot running in September. Is that feasible?
[07:54] Sofia: Yes, if we get prompts and network info this week we can schedule bench and staging access early September.
[08:03] Priya: I'll set up weekly standups — propose Tuesdays 15:00 UTC.
[08:10] Olivia: Works for us.
[08:14] Maya: A minor concern — we sometimes see transcription or model hallucination impacting QA; any mitigation?
[08:22] Liam: We'll build guardrails: deterministic output schemas, function/tool calling, and reranking strategies. Also, Redwood Optimize can flag quality degradation tied to prompt sets.
[08:37] Sanjay: On rollouts — canary percentages and automatic rollback?
[08:42] Sofia: Yes — we support canary deploys with metrics-based rollback rules. We'll help define thresholds.
[08:51] Olivia: Do you have a troubleshooting playbook for when latency spikes?
[08:55] Priya: Yes — runbook includes steps: check regional pool, fallback to smaller model, throttle QPS, and open support escalation.
[09:05] Maya: Are there any limitations around context length? We often have long documents.
[09:12] Liam: Model-dependent; kernel selection and KV cache optimizations can handle longer context with quantization trade-offs. We'll recommend model variants and tokenization strategies.
[09:28] (short pause)
[09:35] Sanjay: Anything else on legal or procurement?
[09:39] Priya: Procurement will get the contract template once they approve SOW; legal might want an NDA extension — we'll share contact.
[09:48] Olivia: Okay next steps recap?
[09:52] Sofia: Recap: Redwood to share security folder (Priya) by 08/27; Indigo to share prompt corpus (Maya) by 08/30; SE bench run scheduled target 09/01; staging access after NDA; weekly cadence Tuesdays 15:00 UTC.
[10:12] Maya: Sounds good — thanks all.
[10:16] Sanjay: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[10:20] Liam: We'll follow up with the bench plan and a short checklist for network pre-reqs.
[10:26] Priya: I'll send calendar invites for the weekly standups and the bench window.
[10:32] Olivia: Thanks everyone.
[10:36] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: some speaker tags auto-generated and occasional background noise. A few product names transcribed slightly off (e.g., 'kv cache' sometimes appears as 'kay vee cache').
